old_title: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Formula One 2026 - live
new_title: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: George Russell holds off Max Verstappen to win - as it happened
old_text:
Lap 8/51: The next task for Verstappen will be to close on Piastri. The Australian hasn't been able to trouble Russell yet; with the Mercedes happily out in front.
As for Antonelli? He has gained a couple of places, but is still down in 14th. A win from here would be astonishing.
Hadjar has allowed Verstappen to overtake him, too, so the Dutchman has gained an incredible five places on his qualifying position; he started P8 and is now third.
A podium surely beckons for him given how much speed he's got. He may have his eyes on a bigger prize.
Lap 6/51: Verstappen has absolutely stormed beyond Leclerc into fourth. What have Red Bull been doing to their cars in the past 24 hours? They look so much faster today than they did in qualifying.
Lap 4/51: Hadjar attempts another move, but cannot get around Leclerc, who had the pace to see off the Red Bull ... well, only for a time. Hadjar eventually gets his man! The Red Bull is into third, behind Piastri and Russell.
His teammate Verstappen seems to have a bit of pace, too.
Lap 3/51: Most of the drivers at the front of the race have chosen soft tyres, other than Russell, Norris and Verstappen, who are on mediums. Hadjar has regained his P4 spot from Norris, and Verstappen has now gone beyond the Brit, but there's a lot of jostling for places at the moment, positions changing all the time.
Norris overtook Hadjar on the straight going into the second lap, a great move by the McLaren. Verstappen sneaks inside Hamilton so climbs into P6, with Hamilton caught off guard, there.
Lap 2/51: Russell leads, then, followed by Piastri, then it's Leclerc, Norris, then Hadjar.
Antonelli is down in 17th, so has actually lost a place, rather than working his way up the field. Plenty of racing to do, of course, and that's the first lap done.
The first corner is upon us very quickly at Baku, and it's Piastri who squeezes ahead of Leclerc to take second spot and Norris is up into third, too. A good start for the McLarens as Russell steers clear of trouble to remain in first.
According to said broadcaster, the winds have dropped in Baku and we're set for rather favourable racing conditions on a track that, although twisty, can lend itself to overtaking well. It's always a gorgeous setting in Baku with the 6km-long track right in the heart of the old city.
Swedish House Mafia is now blaring out on the track, as Russell gets on his Mercedes scooter to head for the track and shares a few - and I mean only a few - words with Sky Sports.
If you want the vibe following at home, go for it:
Fair play, the Azerbaijan anthem is an absolute banger. And it has just been terrifically performed on track.
If you remember, last year, before lights out, George Russell and Lando Norris were seen giggling as a group of local children belted the anthem out with plenty of passion.
We're about to get the anthems and all the pre-race pomp and ceremony. The drivers and teams are making their on-track adjustments before it all starts.
Lando Norris hasn't been a particularly happy bunny this season. He described McLaren's lack of pace as "pretty pants" in the lead-up to this Grand Prix, and fifth on the grid to start the race reflects that mediocre performance by the reigning world champion.
With Piastri qualifying third, can Norris rein in his teammate and finish on the podium this weekend? It would seem doubtful, in truth.
Whether races take place in the Middle East towards the end of the season, or not, could affect this season's F1 world championship. Kimi Antonelli leads his Mercedes teammate George Russell by 81 points with nine meetings remaining, as it stands. If that number was reduced the Italian could close it out even sooner than might be expected.
Formula One is pressing ahead with its original plan to finish the season with races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, although a contingency is understood to be in place to host a final round in Imola if the volatile situation means both meetings have to be cancelled.
"I personally want to go. I love going to the Middle East," said Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. "From what I have read, things seem OK out there, but I don't have all the information and I don't know what the risk levels are. I trust in Stefano [Domenicali, F1's chief executive] to make the right decision for the sport. And I do hope we get to go there."
Is there any chance Kimi Antonelli can win this race from way back on the grid? Well, at Monza he came back from 19th to take victory and Baku, with its long straights, has similarly generous opportunities for overtaking. But he cannot afford to be caught in incidents in the midfield.
"Race smart in the early stages tomorrow and I am sure he has the pace to climb his way back up the field," said the Mercedes deputy team principal, Bradley Lord.
His teammate, George Russell, said: "You can't discount Kimi. You know, started 19th in Monza and now he's in 16th, so, yeah, he should be leading by a few laps early this time." He added: "He's been flawless this season. It's the first mistake he's made in a qualifying or race this whole year."
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix - with a rare Saturday race day for us all to enjoy. The big story from qualifying yesterday was runaway World Championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashing out, meaning he will start today's race 16th on the grid, handing the initiative to his Mercedes teammate George Russell, who claimed pole position.
Antonelli said his crash was "stupid" but also "a good way to come back to earth" after a stunning few weeks for the young Italian driver, who won the Italian and Spanish Grands Prix to take his tally to eight race wins so far this season.
Second fastest in qualifying in Baku was Ferrari's Charles Leclerc second, with Oscar Piastri third.
The race gets under way at 3pm local time in Azerbaijan, which translated to midday UK time. We'll bring you all the relevant buildup, followed by lap-by-lap updates, well near enough anyway. Can Antonelli pull off the improbable in Baku, can Russell close the gap to the championship leader, or can one of the Ferraris or McLarens make an impact? Let's find out.
new_text:
The report from our man Giles Richards has now landed, which means this live blog can conclude. It's been a good day for George Russell in Azerbaijan, though he had to work mightily hard for the race win, coming under severe pressure from Red Bulls Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, who were second and third, after a dramatic finish to the race. Reigning world champion Lando Norris was among those who crashed out.
Kimi Antonelli, who was fifth, loses a bit of ground in the race for this year's world championship. Next stop: Malaysia next weekend!
You may think Verstappen is happy with second, but that's not his mentality.
"We had a good race, it was a bit difficult with the medium tyre, but we had a good restart ... I got close, but it was not enough."
Hadjar says: "I'm happy. It's been a very long six weeks since I enjoyed myself, but I felt strong and I'm very happy for a first proper podium on pure pace. I'm completely satisfied."
Let's hear from the top three finishers, with Russell, Verstappen and Hadjar all speaking to the media. Timo Glock is on the microphone.
Russell says: "It's amazing to be back on the top step of the podium. I'm really proud to have had this weekend. The first half of the race felt pretty plain sailing, Max almost got me on the line, but all-in-all an incredible weekend.
Victory for Russell in Baku - only just after a late charge by Verstappen! A big moment for the Brit in his quest to chase down Mercedes teammate Antonelli in the world championship standings.
The race finished with a yellow flag out after Valtteri Bottas crashed into a barrier.
Russell is the deserved race winner but he was made to sweat right at the end, winning by 0.1 seconds.
Final lap: To be honest, it would now take something of a Devon Loch moment from Russell to squander this race victory. And he's barely looked close to making a mistake this afternoon.
Verstappen still has speed but he just cannot get within striking distance of Russell, with time now running out. Red Bull may have to settle for two podiums for their drivers, without the actual race win.
Lap 47/51: We're at the real business end of this race now and Antonelli has sustained a bit of wing damage, which may impair his ability to climb further up the standings in the time he's got left.
Will the world championship leader settle for fifth?
Russell has looked comfortable for the majority of the race, but Verstappen is giving it absolutely everything to push the Mercedes for the race win. The gap is around half a second, with five laps to go.
Lap 45/51: It's shaping up to be a decent weekend for Haas, whose drivers Ocon and Bearman are in seventh and eighth respectively. They'll be happy to pick up points.
There will be no further action for Lindblad and Liam Lawson for their turn one incident earlier on.
Lap 43/51: That didn't take long! Antonelli is past Hamilton and into fifth. There's a 3.5 second gap to Leclerc in fourth, which may not be insurmountable.
Lap 42/51: This is now an ideal situation for George Russell in his quest for the world championship. He's out in front - though will have to see off Verstappen in the next nine laps - and Antonelli is still down in sixth, though the Italian deserves credit for making up so much ground.
Lap 41/51: The stewards have noted a number of incidents, which happened in those restarts after the safety car was out. It's likely that Colapinto will be in trouble for causing Gasly and Norris to crash out.
Lap 40/51: Verstappen is right into Russell's slipstream down the straight - oh and Piastri locks up trying to defend from Hadjar and finds himself out of the points completely! The Australian has lost loads of places there.
Lap 39/51: Russell holds off Verstappen on the restart, but the Red Bull of Hadjar is pressurising Piastri. Doing something similar to Lewis Hamilton is Kimi Antonelli. The Red Bulls and the Mercedes have the speed right now.
Lap 38/51: To confirm: Gasly and Norris join Alonso, Stroll and Albon in being confirmed DNFs in this race. Somehow Colapinto is able to carry on, although he needs a pit stop with Lawson also OK to continue, although he lost a few positions.
Replays show Colapinto slide into his Alpine teammate Pierre Gasly, who in turn hit Norris, who was trying to get around the outside of the duo. That's very unfortunate for Norris, really. He had nowhere to go.
Liam Lawson was also involved in a crash, hit by his teammate, Lindblad.
The yellow flag is being waved again after that crash, which appeared to have involved Norris. Goodness me, a nightmare for the reigning world champion, who is seen walking over the track and is car is picked up by recovery vehicles.
The recovery team are still clearing things up after Albon's crash and the safety car is still out. Hopefully we get back to racing soon, because I think it could be rather exciting. Patience.
Lap 32/51: They're all back out onto the track and the pack have closed up, with Russell's huge lead pretty much gone. It could make for an exciting finale to the race.
Antonelli quickly pits and gets the soft tyres on; Lando Norris does the same after his lockup. Who will benefit from this safety car and will we get a red flag?
We shall find out soon. The top six still haven't pitted, but Mercedes may bring their race leader Russell in shortly.
Oh no, what's happened to Lando Norris? A big lockup from the McLaren has him spinning in circles on the straight - he's lost positions, taken a big knock to the tyre and will need to box soon.
Lap 27/51: Verstappen is again having to defend some attacks from Hadjar. "Can I go for it, or what?" is the - very relevant - question from the Frenchman, who is advised to "keep it clean" by team engineers.
George Russell is about to lap the back-marker, Valtteri Bottas, which shows how much quicker his Mercedes is than those teams at the back of the grid. It's now a 10-second lead for the British driver, a comfortable day for him, although he's just revealed he "nibbled" the wall on a recent turn. Shouldn't be too much of an issue.
Oh dear, it's not a pit stop for Alonso, the veteran driver is OUT of the race altogether. A double DNF for Aston Martin and a nightmare weekend for them, with major car issues.
Carlos Sainz in the Williams is the first driver to head for the pit lane. Will that trigger others to do the same? We'll see - Alonso is also pitting.
